newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - New low underlines crumbling gold price hopes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - New low underlines crumbling gold price hopes.

text.p: Hopes early this year that gold prices would soar have been crumbling for weeks and they may not have hit the bottom even after bullion reached an 18-month low on Tuesday, market analysts said.
"Negative sentiment has been building up for a while," one analyst said after gold was fixed at $377.05 per ounce, its lowest official fixing since March 6 last year.
The previous day it was set at $379.00 and a month ago it was a relatively healthy $386.90, but still well off the $416.25 set at the peak of a blistering five-week rally on February 2.

That was gold's highest price since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait that started a short-lived dash for protection from inflation, soaring oil prices and currency instability in the tradional safe haven of gold.
"A number of issues are behind gold failing to maintain early levels," another analayst with a major bank said.

"Concerns over inflation through economies overheating have not come through. There was a very large amount of gold hedging (by producers) and then the Belgian Central Bank sales also needed absorbing by the market," he said.
While the 203 tonnes of Belgian gold sold in March and an unquantified amount of forward sales from producers were being absorbed, the price steadily withered from its high.
Another analyst explained the downturn more simply: "At the start of the year a rush of blood to the head was bashed by central bank selling. The market was not as strong as was thought."
Investors, for the most U.S-owned and ultra cash-rich investment funds, quickly decided there were better places to put their money, such as Wall Street stocks.
Physical interest from the price-sensitive gold affinity areas like India, China and South East Asia also vanished due to still relatively high prices and changing fashions.
Japanese gold imports also plunged from 1995 levels.
According to the latest publication from independent research group Gold Fields Mineral Services (GFMS), demand was down 3.7 percent during the 1996 first half at 1,580 tonnes.
In contrast mine production increased for the first time in two years to 1,102 tonnes, up 3.2 percent, confirming that the gap between gold's supply and demand was diminishing.
"A lot of investors lost confidence in gold (after the GFMS data)," an analyst said.

The loss of confidence was on a huge scale. The investment funds turned their "long" --- holding gold -- positions to "shorts" -- selling gold they did not own at today's price in the expectation that the market would fall, allowing them to buy at a cheaper price before delivery was due.
Official figures showed last week the investors had built a total of 5.7 million oz short positions on the Comex gold futures market.
"There is very little to provide encouragement for the funds to take out any (long) positions. Negative news just reinforces this view ," an analyst at a major London-based bank said.
Shivers also went through the market from recent talks at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on plans to sell five million ounces from IMF reserves to aid poor countries.
"The IMF is not going to go away. At some point the potential for a sale is there. How much and when they will not say for some time," the analyst added.
The combination of fund selling and potential IMF selling was enough to hit prices again. But demand remained flat.

"Now consumers are waiting to buy, creating effectively another short positions. All around we are seeing shorts and it is a bit like last December," one analyst said referring to the market's very negative stance last year just before the rally.

This analyst added: "I'm still pretty confident. The downside risk is getting less and less and the risk of something triggering a bit of short covering given the size of these shorts (is increasing)," he said.
"There could be enough short covering potential to get it back up to $390 or perhaps even further," the analyst said.

Others were less convinced. "We expect prices to weaken further and test the lows. In early January we were quoting a range for the year of $374-$420 so now we hope the lower level will hold," another leading analyst said.
"We are extremely pessimistic for gold. Low inflation and low interest rates mean there is nothing there for gold but by the middle of next year it may be different," he added.
